target.title: fix(discord): retry stale preview cleanup after final delivery
target.body:
Closes #104865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users with partial streaming could see a stale preview beside the fresh final reply when preview cleanup failed transiently.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview ownership is now cleared only after DELETE succeeds. Discord teardown performs one bounded cleanup retry when a fresh final was delivered but an unfinalized preview ID remains; previews finalized in place are still preserved.

This keeps retry policy at the existing lifecycle boundaries. It does not add timers, configuration, background queues, or additional final-message sends.

## User Impact

Transient Discord preview cleanup failures get one recovery attempt during normal turn teardown instead of immediately becoming unrecoverable stale messages. Final replies are still delivered exactly once.

Mattermost uses the shared helper and now also retains failed preview IDs for a later cleanup call.

## Evidence

### RED → GREEN

- Shared lifecycle regressions:
  - first DELETE rejects;
  - preview ID remains owned;
  - second clear retries DELETE and clears ownership on success;
  - if ownership advances while the old DELETE is in flight, compare-and-clear preserves the replacement preview ID.
- Discord process regression:
  - fresh final delivery succeeds once;
  - first preview clear retains the ID;
  - teardown invokes one second clear;
  - preview ID is then cleared.

Both tests failed on current `main` (`9a04fb40ce`) for the expected reasons before the implementation changes, then passed afterward.

### Live Discord proof

Redacted live run on exact head `5582df93dfe17ac4ec3d8c39dc3d9a857a9f5bf5`: [Crabbox run `run_4627a4bad139`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4627a4bad139).

- Isolated public-network Crabbox; no instance role, Tailscale, or hydrated credentials.
- Created a real Discord preview successfully.
- Replaced only the first preview DELETE response with a controlled HTTP 500; the preview ID remained owned.
- Delivered exactly one real final Discord reply.
- Teardown made exactly one retry; that DELETE reached Discord.
- After cleanup, live Discord GET returned 404 for the preview and 200 for the final reply.
- The final reply was then deleted by the harness cleanup block.

The evidence omits credentials, broker data, guild/channel/application/message IDs, and message content. The first 500 is controlled fault injection because a transient Discord 5xx cannot be requested deterministically; the retry and both postconditions are live Discord API results.

Accessible redacted diagnostic manifest (also emitted by the linked run):


The four failed compact shards do not execute this PR's Discord or shared draft-stream files.

- Three failures are the same terminal-main-session regression on `main`: [`commands-agent-channel`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29177865868/job/86610331155), [`gateway-methods`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29177865868/job/86610331637), and [`auto-reply-reply-session`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29177865868/job/86610332030). target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

The same zero-duration hazard applies to `session.maintenance.pruneAfter` — it accepts `"0h"` / `0`, resolves to `0ms`, and produces a current-time cleanup cutoff that deletes all non-preserved sessions.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` for both `pruneAfter` and `resetArchiveRetention` to reject any string or number that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false` for `resetArchiveRetention`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Two field-specific legacy rules with accurate per-field diagnostics. Uses `normalizeStringifiedOptionalString` + `parseDurationMs` to handle all parser-equivalent zero representations including numeric `0`. One migration spec covers both fields with independent one-pass repair:
- `pruneAfter` zero → removes value, restores **30d session-pruning default**
- `resetArchiveRetention` zero → removes value, restores **indefinite retention** (disk-budget eviction only)

### Files changed (4 files)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | zero-duration rejection for both fields |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | two parser-backed rules + independent two-field repair |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | 27 focused tests |

- **Commands / artifacts**:

target.title: fix(openrouter): apply request policy to music generation requests

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating music through OpenRouter could configure provider request policy, such as custom headers or proxy settings, but the OpenRouter music generation HTTP request ignored that policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter music provider now sanitizes `cfg.models.providers.openrouter.request` and passes it into the existing provider HTTP resolver for the music generation request path. The change stays limited to music generation request configuration and leaves model selection, streaming, timeout, and response parsing behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users who rely on provider-level request settings can expect OpenRouter music generation to honor the same configured transport policy as the other OpenRouter media path. Default behavior is unchanged when no request policy is configured.

target.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

Adds Phase 0 support for the MCP Apps extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`) to OpenClaw's generic bundle MCP client and Control UI. Any configured MCP server can bind a tool to a `ui://` resource through `_meta.ui.resourceUri`; no server-specific host integration is required.

The official Excalidraw MCP App server is the conformance target. The external proof-of-concept plugin remains out of tree at [fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin).

## What changed

### Generic MCP Apps runtime

- Declares the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` client capability for `text/html;profile=mcp-app`.
- Parses nested and legacy flat `_meta.ui` declarations and reads bound `ui://` resources after successful tool calls.
- Filters app-only tools (`_meta.ui.visibility` without `model`) from agent exposure.
- Preserves the normal text/structured tool result for non-UI surfaces.

### Durable, bounded view storage

- Stores complete app view snapshots outside transcripts in the shared OpenClaw state SQLite database.
- Persists only an opaque, validated descriptor in `details.mcpApp`; app HTML, tool input, and tool result do not inflate `chat.history`.
- Enforces 30-day retention, 128 views, 256 MiB total, and 8 MiB per payload, including all persisted string fields.
- Physically deletes expired rows during lookup and prunes oldest rows on insertion.
- Invalid, expired, or evicted descriptors fail closed.

### Production Control UI host

- Resolves descriptors through a ticket-protected, no-store Gateway resource endpoint.
- Uses the MCP Apps double-frame sandbox pattern: an opaque-origin outer proxy and a nested `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` app frame.
- Applies the app-declared CSP in the proxy response and does not delegate camera, microphone, geolocation, or clipboard permissions.
- Renders the app inline even while the enclosing tool disclosure is collapsed.
- Keeps the same iframe and request stable across ordinary chat rerenders.
- Survives Gateway restart plus page reload without rerunning the MCP tool.
- Offers an explicit page reload when an already-open tab holds a stale process ticket or a stored view cannot be resolved.

### Plugin surface

- Native plugin manifests can declare `mcpServers`, merged through the enabled-bundle path.
- User configuration wins by server name; disabling a plugin detaches its declared server.

## Security model

- App documents and MCP metadata remain untrusted input.
- The outer sandbox has an opaque origin; the inner same-origin capability is confined to the opaque proxy document.
- App CSP origins and permissions are validated before use.
- App-initiated host requests such as `tools/call` and `ui/open-link` receive JSON-RPC method-not-found in Phase 0.
- Resource lookup requires both the process-scoped ticket and an unguessable 192-bit view ID.

## Verification

- Live Rosita/Tailscale proof with the real Excalidraw MCP App: created the OpenClaw plugin architecture diagram, kept it visible under a collapsed tool row, restarted the Gateway, reloaded the existing conversation, and recovered the same editable app without rerunning the tool.
- Live `chat.history` proof: the persisted MCP App descriptor serialized to 149 bytes and contained only `viewId`, `serverName`, `toolName`, and `resourceUri`.
- AWS Crabbox (`cbx_100691b2e58d`, `c7a.8xlarge`):
  - [436 focused tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_36e1d9a26aaa)
  - [final storage retention/bounds tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3440977bb7b5)
  - [final Chromium MCP App E2E passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fb2774cc9f5c), including stable iframe identity, single-fetch behavior across rerenders, production CSP handshake, and reload recovery UI
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm db:kysely:check`
- focused agent, Gateway, history-projection, HTTP, UI extraction, and materialization suites
- `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`
- final `gpt-5.6-sol` autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings

## Current limit

Phase 0 is view-only for app-to-host calls. A full host bridge for app-initiated tool calls and navigation remains follow-up work.

## Release-note context

The Control UI can now render generic MCP App tool interfaces securely and restore them after reloads or Gateway restarts, while keeping large app payloads out of chat transcripts.
